sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or give reasons).

questions.q: Identify the activities as Money Income (MI), Real Income (RI), Need (N) or Desire (D). (i) Getting free petrol allowance from the company (ii) Purchasing a new video game (iii) Interest received from a fixed deposit (iv) Purchasing medicines during illness.
questions.answer: (i) Real income (RI). (ii) Desire (D). (iii) Money income (MI). (iv) Need (N).

questions.q: Mention four investment schemes which offer liquidity.
questions.answer: Savings bank account, post office savings account, units of UTI and gold or property (which can be sold).

questions.q: Write any four advantages of saving.
questions.answer: A secure future after retirement, meeting emergencies, fulfilling family goals and raising the standard of living (or starting a small business).

questions.q: Match Column A with Column B. A: (a) General Provident Fund (b) Debentures. B: (i) Loan to a company at fixed interest (ii) Compulsory saving for salaried employees (iii) Part ownership of a company.
State True or False. (a) Making pickles for your family is real income. (b) Income management is useful only when income is large.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: it is needed at every income level.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Ritu sells pickles to support her family and has also kept a paying guest. Identify this income and give two suggestions to increase it.
questions.answer: This is money income from an income generating activity and from renting part of the house. She can take bulk orders and sell through shops, and use the spare room for more paying guests.

or.q: Ravi grows his own vegetables behind his house and uses public transport. Identify these incomes and give two suggestions to increase them.
or.answer: Growing vegetables is real income (goods) and using public transport saves money, also a real income. He can grow more vegetables and use the surplus and share transport or walk for short trips.

questions.q: What is meant by income management? Name its steps.
questions.answer: It is the planned and controlled use of the family income. The steps are planning the use of income with savings and controlling the expenditure.

questions.q: List two advantages of keeping money in a post office.
questions.answer: Post offices are conveniently located and an account can be started with a very small amount. Interest in many schemes is exempt from income tax.

questions.q: Distinguish between needs and desires.
questions.answer: Needs are requirements that must be met, such as food, clothing and shelter. Desires are things we wish to have but which are not necessary for life.

questions.q: What is meant by supplementing family income? Give two ways.
questions.answer: It means adding to the regular income. Examples are an income generating activity at home and a part-time job.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the guidelines for preparing an expenditure plan (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Divide the money income among areas such as food, clothing, housing, education and savings. (ii) Meet primary needs first, then secondary needs, then comforts and luxuries. (iii) Keep enough for each area for the full month and keep expenditure below income so that savings are possible.

questions.q: Explain the advantages of maintaining a record of income and expenditure (three points).
questions.answer: (i) It shows exactly how much is spent and on what. (ii) It checks unnecessary spending and allows comparison of different months. (iii) It helps in future planning and shows market trends through the rate column.

questions.q: Explain the factors to be considered while selecting an investment scheme (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Capacity to save, safety and a higher rate of interest. (ii) Easy liquidity and other benefits such as tax relief. (iii) Purchasing power above inflation and a convenient place.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain any five investment avenues with their advantages.
questions.answer: (i) Bank: safe, interest, withdrawal and loans against fixed deposits. (ii) Post office: convenient, small amounts, tax-free interest in NSC. (iii) Provident Fund: compulsory saving, tax exemption and loans (GPF and PPF). (iv) Life insurance: safe, financial protection for dependents, tax relief and forced saving. (v) UTI units: regular dividend, tax relief and can be encashed. (vi) Shares and debentures: shares give possible high returns with risk; debentures give a fixed interest with more safety.
